en: Majjhima Nikāya 118 Ānāpānassati Sutta:
Mindfulness of Breathing Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in the Eastern Park, in the Mansion of Migāra’s Mother, together with many well-known and renowned elder disciples:
with the Venerable Sāriputta, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna, the Venerable Mahākassapa, the Venerable Mahākaccāyana,
the Venerable Mahākoṭṭhika, the Venerable Mahākappina, and the Venerable...
And together with Mahācunda, the Venerable Anuruddha, the Venerable Revata, the Venerable Ānanda,
and other well-known elder disciples.
At that time, the elder bhikkhus were exhorting and instructing the junior bhikkhus.
Some elder bhikkhus exhort and instruct ten bhikkhus;
some elder bhikkhus exhort and instruct twenty bhikkhus; some elder bhikkhus exhort and instruct thirty bhikkhus;
some elder bhikkhus exhort and instruct forty bhikkhus.
And those newly ordained monks, being exhorted and instructed by the elder monks, came to know a sublime distinction between what was before and what was after.
Now at that time, on the Uposatha day of the fifteenth, on the full moon night of the Pavāraṇā ceremony, the Blessed One was seated in the open air surrounded by the Saṅgha of monks.
Then the Blessed One, having surveyed the silent Saṅgha of monks one by one, addressed the monks:
“I am intent upon this practice, monks;
my mind is set upon this practice, monks.
Therefore, monks, exert even more energy for the attainment of the unattained, for the reaching of the unreached, and for the realization of the unrealized.”
"I shall indeed wait right here in Sāvatthī for the Komudī Cātumāsinī festival.
The monks of the countryside heard:
"The Blessed One, it seems, will wait right there in Sāvatthī for the Komudī Cātumāsinī festival."
Those country monks were descending upon Sāvatthī to see the Blessed One.
And those elder monks were, to an even greater extent, exhorting and instructing the newly ordained monks.
Some elder monks exhorted and instructed ten monks; some elder monks [exhorted and instructed]...
Twenty bhikkhus exhort and instruct; some elder bhikkhus exhort and instruct thirty bhikkhus;
some elder bhikkhus exhort and instruct forty bhikkhus.
And those junior bhikkhus, being exhorted and instructed by the elder bhikkhus, perceive a sublime distinction between what was before and what comes after.
Now at that time, on the Uposatha day of the fifteenth, on the full-moon night of the Komudī Cātumāsī festival, the Blessed One was seated in the open air surrounded by the community of monks.
Then the Blessed One, having surveyed the silent community of monks, addressed the monks:
"Monks, this assembly is free from chaff; monks, this assembly is devoid of chaff; it is pure and established in the essence."

“Such, monks, is this Saṅgha of bhikkhus; such, monks, is this assembly—as an assembly that is worthy of gifts, worthy of hospitality, worthy of offerings, worthy of reverential salutation, an unsurpassed field of merit for the world.
Such, monks, is this Saṅgha of bhikkhus; such, monks, is this assembly.”
In such an assembly, what is given in small measure becomes great, and what is given in great measure becomes even greater.
Such, monks, is this Saṅgha of bhikkhus; such, monks, is this assembly—an assembly such as is rare for the world to behold.
"Monks, such is this Saṅgha of bhikkhus; such is this assembly, monks, that it is worth traveling many leagues to see, even with a shoulder bag.

Monks, there are bhikkhus in this Saṅgha who are arahants, whose taints are destroyed, who have lived the holy life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained their own goal, utterly destroyed the fetters of existence, and are completely liberated through final knowledge."
"Monks, there are indeed such monks in this Saṅgha of monks. There are, monks, monks in this Saṅgha of monks who,
through the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, are of spontaneous birth, attaining final Nibbāna there, not subject to returning from that world—
such monks, indeed, are found in this Saṅgha of monks."

“Bhikkhus, there are bhikkhus in this Saṅgha of bhikkhus who, with the complete destruction of three fetters and the attenuation of lust, hate, and delusion, are once-returners; having returned to this world only once more, they will make an end of suffering—such bhikkhus, indeed, are found in this Saṅgha of bhikkhus.

Bhikkhus, there are bhikkhus in this Saṅgha of bhikkhus who, with the complete destruction of three fetters, are stream-enterers, no longer subject to rebirth in the lower worlds, fixed in destiny, and bound for full enlightenment.”
"Monks, there are indeed such bhikkhus in this Saṅgha of bhikkhus. There are, monks,
bhikkhus in this Saṅgha of bhikkhus who dwell devoted to the practice of developing the four foundations of mindfulness—
monks, there are indeed such bhikkhus in this Saṅgha of bhikkhus."
"There are, monks, monks in this Saṅgha of monks who dwell devoted to the cultivation and practice of the four right efforts … [and so on] … the four bases of psychic power … the five faculties …"
They dwell devoted to the practice of the development of the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the noble eightfold path.
"Monks, there are indeed such monks in this Saṅgha of monks.
There are, monks, monks in this Saṅgha of monks who dwell devoted to the practice of the development of loving-kindness; ...
who dwell devoted to the practice of the development of compassion; ..."

They dwell devoted to the practice of the cultivation of sympathetic joy… they dwell devoted to the practice of the cultivation of equanimity… they dwell devoted to the practice of the cultivation of foulness…
They dwell devoted to the practice of developing the perception of impermanence—
such monks, bhikkhus, are found in this Saṅgha of bhikkhus.
There are, bhikkhus, monks in this Saṅgha of bhikkhus who dwell devoted to the practice of developing mindfulness of breathing.
“Monks, mindfulness of breathing, when developed and cultivated, is of great fruit and great benefit.
Mindfulness of breathing, monks, when developed and cultivated, fulfills the four foundations of mindfulness.
The four foundations of mindfulness, when developed and cultivated, fulfill the seven factors of enlightenment.”
The seven factors of enlightenment, when developed and cultivated, fulfill true knowledge and liberation.
And how, monks, is mindfulness of breathing developed and cultivated so that it is of great fruit and great benefit?
Here, monks, a monk, having gone to the forest, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut, sits down; having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect, and established mindfulness before him.
Thus, being mindful, he breathes in; being mindful, he breathes out.
Breathing in long, he knows: “I am breathing in long”; or breathing out long, he knows:
“I am breathing out long. Breathing in short, he knows: “I am breathing in short”; or breathing out short, he knows: “I am breathing out short.”
He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in experiencing the whole body’; he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out experiencing the whole body.
He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in tranquilizing the bodily formation’; he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out tranquilizing the bodily formation.
He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in experiencing rapture’; he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out experiencing rapture.’
He trains thus: ‘Experiencing pleasure, I shall breathe in’; he trains thus: ‘Experiencing pleasure, I shall breathe out.
He trains thus: ‘Experiencing the mental formations, I shall breathe in’; he trains thus: ‘Experiencing the mental formations, I shall breathe out.
He trains thus: ‘Tranquillizing the mental formations, I shall breathe in’; he trains thus: ‘Tranquillizing the mental formations, I shall breathe out.’
He trains thus: ‘Experiencing the mind, I shall breathe in’; he trains thus: ‘Experiencing the mind, I shall breathe out.
He trains thus: ‘Gladdening the mind, I shall breathe in’; he trains thus: ‘Gladdening the mind, I shall breathe out.
He trains thus: ‘Concentrating the mind, I shall breathe in’; he trains thus: ‘Concentrating the mind, I shall breathe out.’
He trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in liberating the mind’; he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out liberating the mind.
He trains thus: ‘Contemplating impermanence, I shall breathe in’; he trains thus: ‘Contemplating impermanence, I shall breathe out.
He trains thus: ‘Contemplating dispassion, I shall breathe in’; he trains thus: ‘Contemplating dispassion, I shall breathe out.’
‘I shall breathe in contemplating cessation,’ he trains himself; ‘I shall breathe out contemplating cessation,’ he trains himself.
‘I shall breathe in contemplating relinquishment,’ he trains himself; ‘I shall breathe out contemplating relinquishment,’ he trains himself.
Thus developed, monks, thus cultivated, mindfulness of breathing is of great fruit and great benefit.
And how, monks, is mindfulness of breathing developed and cultivated so that it fulfills the four foundations of mindfulness?
At whatever time, monks, a monk, breathing in long, understands: ‘I am breathing in long’; or breathing out long, understands:
‘I am breathing out long’; or breathing in short, understands: ‘I am breathing in short’; or breathing out short, understands: ‘I am breathing out short’—
‘Experiencing the whole body, I shall breathe in,’ he trains himself; ‘experiencing the whole body, I shall breathe out,’ he trains himself;
‘tranquillizing the bodily formation, I shall breathe in,’ he trains himself; ‘tranquillizing the bodily formation, I shall breathe out,’ he trains himself.
At that time, monks, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world.
“Bhikkhus, among the bodies, I say that one is a certain body, namely, in-breathing and out-breathing.
Therefore, bhikkhus, on that occasion a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world.
Bhikkhus, on whatever occasion a bhikkhu trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in experiencing rapture,’ he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out experiencing rapture.’”
He trains thus: ‘Experiencing pleasure, I shall breathe in’; he trains thus: ‘Experiencing pleasure, I shall breathe out.
He trains thus: ‘Experiencing the mental formations, I shall breathe in’; he trains thus: ‘Experiencing the mental formations, I shall breathe out.
He trains thus: ‘Tranquilizing the mental formations, I shall breathe in’; he trains thus: ‘Tranquilizing the mental formations, I shall breathe out.’
“Bhikkhus, on that occasion a bhikkhu dwells contemplating feelings in feelings, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world.
I say, bhikkhus, that among the various kinds of feelings, this is one: namely, careful attention to in-breathing and out-breathing.

Therefore, bhikkhus, on that occasion a bhikkhu dwells contemplating feelings in feelings, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world.”
At whatever time, monks, a monk trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in experiencing the mind’; he trains thus:
‘I shall breathe out experiencing the mind’; he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in gladdening the mind’; he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out gladdening the mind’;
he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in concentrating the mind’; he trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out concentrating the mind’;
‘I shall breathe in liberating the mind,’ he trains himself; ‘I shall breathe out liberating the mind,’ he trains himself.
On that occasion, monks, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the mind in the mind, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world.
Monks, I do not say that one who is muddled in mindfulness and lacking clear comprehension possesses mindfulness of breathing.
"Therefore, monks, on that occasion a monk dwells contemplating the mind in the mind, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world.
Monks, on whatever occasion a monk trains thus: ‘I shall breathe in contemplating impermanence,’ and trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out contemplating impermanence’; he trains thus:
‘I shall breathe in contemplating dispassion,’ and trains thus: ‘I shall breathe out contemplating dispassion’..."
‘I shall breathe in contemplating cessation,’ he trains himself; ‘I shall breathe out contemplating cessation,’ he trains himself.
‘I shall breathe in contemplating relinquishment,’ he trains himself; ‘I shall breathe out contemplating relinquishment,’ he trains himself.
At that time, monks, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world.
Thus, having seen with wisdom that very abandoning of covetousness and dejection, he dwells having thoroughly looked on with equanimity.
Therefore, monks, at that time a monk dwells contemplating phenomena among phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and dejection regarding the world.
It is in this way, monks, that mindfulness of breathing, when developed and cultivated in this manner, fulfills the four foundations of mindfulness.
And how, monks, are the four foundations of mindfulness developed and cultivated so that they fulfill the seven factors of enlightenment?

At whatever time, monks, a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world—at that time his mindfulness is established and unconfused.
At whatever time, monks, a monk’s mindfulness is established and unconfused, the mindfulness factor of enlightenment [is fulfilled].
At that time, the bhikkhu’s energy is aroused. At that time, the bhikkhu develops the mindfulness enlightenment factor;
at that time, the mindfulness enlightenment factor reaches fulfillment of its development in the bhikkhu.
Abiding thus mindful, he investigates, examines, and scrutinizes that phenomenon with wisdom.

At whatever time, monks, a bhikkhu dwelling thus mindfully investigates, scrutinizes, and applies thorough examination to that phenomenon with wisdom, at that time the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena has been undertaken by the bhikkhu;
at that time the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena; [this is] the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena.
At that time, the bhikkhu’s development reaches fulfillment.
As he investigates, scrutinizes, and examines that phenomenon with wisdom, his energy becomes aroused and unflagging.
Monks, when a bhikkhu investigates, scrutinizes, and examines that phenomenon with wisdom...
As he enters upon it, energy is aroused in him, unflagging; at that time the enlightenment factor of energy is aroused in the bhikkhu,
at that time the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of energy, and at that time the enlightenment factor of energy reaches fulfillment by development in the bhikkhu.
For one who has aroused energy, spiritual rapture arises that is not worldly.
Monks, at whatever time spiritual rapture that is not worldly arises for a monk who has aroused energy, at that time the enlightenment factor of rapture is aroused in that monk;
at that time the monk develops the enlightenment factor of rapture.
At that time, the factor of enlightenment of rapture reaches fulfillment through development for the bhikkhu.
When one’s mind is filled with rapture, the body becomes tranquil and the mind also becomes tranquil.
Monks, at whatever time the body of a bhikkhu whose mind is filled with rapture becomes tranquil and the mind also becomes tranquil—
At that time, the enlightenment factor of tranquility has been undertaken by the bhikkhu;
at that time, the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of tranquility; at that time, the enlightenment factor of tranquility reaches fulfillment through development in the bhikkhu.
For one whose body is tranquil and who is happy, the mind becomes concentrated.

“Bhikkhus, at whatever time a bhikkhu’s mind becomes concentrated when his body is tranquil and he is happy, at that time the enlightenment factor of concentration is undertaken by that bhikkhu; at that time the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of concentration;
at that time the enlightenment factor of concentration reaches fulfillment through development in that bhikkhu.”
Thus he thoroughly looks on with equanimity at the mind so well concentrated.

Monks, at whatever time a monk thoroughly looks on with equanimity at the mind so well concentrated, at that time the enlightenment factor of equanimity is aroused in that monk; at that time the enlightenment factor of equanimity... [is established].
At that time, the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity; at that time, the enlightenment factor of equanimity reaches fulfillment through development for that bhikkhu.

At whatever time, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu [dwells contemplating] feelings … mind … [and mental phenomena] … [at that time, the enlightenment factor of equanimity reaches fulfillment through development for that bhikkhu].

He dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world. At that time, mindfulness is established and unconfused for him.
Bhikkhus, at whatever time a bhikkhu’s mindfulness is established and unconfused, at that time the enlightenment factor of mindfulness has been undertaken by that bhikkhu;
at that time the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of mindfulness.
At that time, the factor of enlightenment that is mindfulness reaches fulfillment through development for the bhikkhu.
Dwelling thus mindful, he investigates, examines, and applies investigative scrutiny to that phenomenon with wisdom.
Monks, at whatever time a bhikkhu, dwelling thus mindful, investigates that phenomenon with wisdom...
When he investigates and applies thorough examination, at that time the factor of enlightenment of investigation of phenomena is undertaken by the bhikkhu;

at that time the bhikkhu develops the factor of enlightenment of investigation of phenomena; at that time the factor of enlightenment of investigation of phenomena reaches fulfillment of its development for the bhikkhu.
As he investigates, scrutinizes, and examines that Dhamma with wisdom, his energy becomes aroused and unflagging. Monks,
at whatever time a monk’s energy is aroused and unflagging as he investigates, scrutinizes, and examines that Dhamma with wisdom,
at that time the enlightenment factor of energy is present for that monk.
At that time, the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of energy;
at that time, the enlightenment factor of energy reaches fulfillment through development in the bhikkhu.
In one who has aroused energy, spiritual rapture arises.
“Bhikkhus, at whatever time non-sensual rapture arises in a bhikkhu who has aroused energy, on that occasion the enlightenment factor of rapture is initiated in that bhikkhu;
on that occasion the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of rapture;
on that occasion the enlightenment factor of rapture reaches fulfillment by development in that bhikkhu.”
When one is joyful, the body becomes tranquil and the mind also becomes tranquil.

Monks, at whatever time a monk who is joyful experiences tranquility of both body and mind, at that time the enlightenment factor of tranquility has been initiated by that monk; it is the enlightenment factor of tranquility.
At that time, the bhikkhu develops [it]; at that time, the factor of enlightenment that is tranquility reaches fulfillment through development for the bhikkhu.
For one whose body is tranquil and who is happy, the mind becomes concentrated.
Monks, when the mind of a bhikkhu whose body is tranquil and who is happy becomes concentrated, [at that time...]
At that time, the enlightenment factor of concentration is undertaken by the bhikkhu; at that time, the bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of concentration;
at that time, the enlightenment factor of concentration reaches fulfillment through development in the bhikkhu.
He thoroughly looks on with equanimity at the mind thus concentrated.
At whatever time, monks, a monk thoroughly looks on with equanimity at the mind thus concentrated, at that time the enlightenment factor of equanimity is undertaken by the monk;
at that time the monk develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity; at that time the enlightenment factor of equanimity reaches fulfillment through development for the monk.
“Monks, when the four foundations of mindfulness are thus developed and thus cultivated, they fulfill the seven factors of enlightenment.
And how, monks, are the seven factors of enlightenment developed and how are they cultivated so that they fulfill true knowledge and liberation?
Here, monks, a monk develops the factor of enlightenment that is mindfulness, based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and resulting in relinquishment.”
He develops the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena … [as before] … he develops the enlightenment factor of energy … he develops the enlightenment factor of rapture …
He develops the enlightenment factor of tranquility … he develops the enlightenment factor of concentration … he develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity,
which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and results in relinquishment.
“Monks, when the seven factors of awakening have been developed in this way and cultivated extensively in this way, they fulfill true knowledge and liberation.
Thus spoke the Blessed One.
Delighted, those monks rejoiced in the words of the Blessed One.
The Discourse on Mindfulness of Breathing is finished; it is the eighth.
